hook.say: three weeks in, and today the story goes back to the very beginning. can i ask you something? do you ever have a dream that stays with you after you wake?
options: then you’ll like this queen. listen.
those are the ones that matter. listen.
then let me tell you one people have remembered for two thousand years.

steps.line: In the city of Kapilavatthu, Queen Maya, wife of King Suddhodana, lay down to sleep one night in the palace.
She dreamed that four guardian spirits lifted her bed and carried her to the mountains, where she was bathed in a still lake and laid on a heavenly couch.

steps.q: Then a white elephant comes toward her in the dream. What does it carry in its trunk?
steps.why: A white lotus. In Buddhist art, the lotus often stands for a heart that stays pure.

steps.line: A white elephant with six tusks came down from a golden mountain, a white lotus in its trunk. It circled her three times, and seemed to enter her right side.

steps.q: Why was a white elephant such a grand sign in old India? Think of who rode one.
steps.why: Airavata, Indra’s great white elephant, is often shown with many tusks. A white elephant meant royalty and rain: greatness, and blessing.

steps.line: In the morning she told the king. He called the wise men who read signs. “Be glad,” they said. “The queen will have a son.”
“If he stays home, he’ll be a great king who rules the world. If he leaves home, he’ll be a buddha, one who wakes up.”

steps.q: You’re King Suddhodana. You want a great king, not a wandering monk. What would you do?
o: Keep every sad sight away from him
Send him early to study with sages
Tell him the prophecy and let him choose
steps.why: That’s what the later stories say he did: palaces, no sickness, no old age in sight. It only made the first glimpse hit harder.

steps.q: The stories go on: where was the baby born?
o: In the palace, with the wise men
At her parents’ house, far away
In a garden, under a tree
steps.why: In the Lumbini garden, on her way to her parents’ home, holding a tree branch, the stories say. Lumbini is in Nepal, and pilgrims still go.

steps.line: Today, a couple tapes a first scan photo to the fridge. Before a child is born, people are already dreaming about who they’ll be.
steps.label: today

say: to be honest about where this comes from: the oldest discourses tell of his conception with a great light and the earth trembling, but no elephant. the dream comes from later life stories and commentaries, and it’s old in its own right. it’s carved in stone at early buddhist sites in india.

every school tells it. in thailand and myanmar, white elephants were long treasured as royal and lucky. in tibetan and nepali painting, the descent into the mother’s womb is one of the twelve great deeds of the buddha’s life.

steps.q: The oldest texts have no elephant, yet the dream is told everywhere. What does that suggest?
o: Later Buddhists made the whole story up
A picture can carry what plain words can’t
The old texts lost most of his life
steps.why: A story can be later and still be beloved. It says, in pictures, what the plain texts say in words: something rare was coming.

today.say: today, think of something good that came into your life before you understood it: a person, a place, a change. some things announce themselves. thank it, quietly.
options: then hold it a moment. that’s enough.
that’s okay. sometimes they only show up looking back.

tomorrow.title: The emperor at Lumbini
tomorrow.line: centuries later, an emperor walks to the garden where the buddha was born, and leaves a stone.
